newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RANGERS MARCH ON TOWARDS NINTH SUCCESSIVE TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RANGERS MARCH ON TOWARDS NINTH SUCCESSIVE TITLE.

text.p: Rangers continued on their seemingly inexorable path towards a ninth successive Scottish championship as goals from Gordon Durie, Jorg Albertz and Brian Laudrup gave them a comfortable 3-0 win at Dunfermline on Saturday.
Victory took them to 64 points, seven clear of Celtic, their only possible challengers, with just 10 premier division matches remaining for each of them.
Durie gave the champions a first half lead and Albertz and Laudrup put the result beyond doubt with two goals in the space of eight minutes midway through the second half.

At the other end of the table second from last Kilmarnock's troubles increased as they went down 2-0 away to Hearts but Motherwell's relegation worries eased slightly as they battled back from two goals down for a 2-2 draw at home to Aberdeen.
In a strongly contested final quarter, both teams were reduced to 10 men as Motherwell's John Philoben and Aberdeen's Dean Windass were sent off and Motherwell were twice denied claims for a penalty.

Aberdeen scored twice in the first half through Billy Dodds and an own goal by Brian Martin but Willie Falconer headed home from a corner in the 48th minute and then in the 54th Alex Burns hit the equaliser.
